readerTitle: Twice the customers, the same profit
caseNote: 가상 사례 (가정 청소 업체, 기장 대행 회사) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 성장은 매출이 느는 것이고, 규모의 이익은 비용이 매출보다 느리게 늘 때만 생긴다. 판단 기준은 '추가 매출 1달러가 남기는 추가 이익'이다.
misconception: 건당 이익이 나는 사업이라면 두 배로 키우면 이익도 두 배가 된다.

sources.text: 관리회계의 표준 개념 (변동비, 계단식 고정비, 영업 레버리지)

factChecks.note: 기장 대행 사례(직원당 고객 25곳 → 35곳)는 설명용 가정이며 실제 업계 평균이 아닙니다.

cards.title: Twice the customers, the same profit
body: A home cleaning company grew from 8 cleaners to 16 in two years. Revenue doubled, from $400,000 to $800,000.
Profit stayed at $60,000. Nobody wasted money. Every job still made money. So where did the growth go?

image.label: Revenue bar doubling while profit bar stays the same
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 왼쪽과 오른쪽에 청소 밴과 청소 도구. 위로 "Revenue" 막대가 두 배로 커지지만 그 아래 "Profit" 막대는 똑같은 높이. 실제 회사 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: What happens to profit if you double?
body: You have 8 cleaners. Each brings in $50,000 a year and costs $30,000 in wages. Profit is $60,000.

At 16 cleaners you'd need an operations manager ($70,000) and more storage and scheduling ($30,000). New clients live farther out, so supplies and travel rise from 10% to 12.5% of revenue. Profit at 16 cleaners will be about…

options.text: $120,000. Double the team, double the profit
options.feedback: This assumes every cost grows neatly with revenue. The manager and storage are new costs you didn't have at all before.

options.text: More than $120,000, because the office costs get spread wider
options.feedback: Right that the original $60,000 of overhead stays put. But the new manager, space and longer drives eat more than that saving.
Yes. The extra $400,000 of revenue brings almost exactly $400,000 of extra cost. The next card shows where it goes.

cards.title: Where the extra $400,000 went
body: Margin fell from 15% to 7.5%. The business got bigger. It didn't get better.

cards.title: Scaling profitably
body: **Scaling profitably** means growing so that costs rise more slowly than revenue. Each new dollar of revenue then keeps more than the dollars before it.
A simple test: extra profit ÷ extra revenue. Here it's $0 ÷ $400,000 = 0%. The company grew. It didn't scale.

image.label: Two lines: revenue rising faster than costs
image.brief: 단순한 선 그래프 2개 나란히. 왼쪽 "Growth": 매출선과 비용선이 나란히 올라감. 오른쪽 "Scale": 매출선이 비용선보다 가파르게 올라가며 사이 간격(이익)이 벌어짐. 간격에 "Profit" 라벨.

cards.softwareNote: Copying software costs almost nothing, so it looks built to scale. But custom features for big clients, hands-on onboarding and a growing sales team can rise in step with revenue, just like cleaners' wages.

cards.title: Three ways costs behave as you grow
body: When sales grow, every cost does one of three things.
list: **In step:** grows with each job, like wages and supplies
**In jumps:** stays flat, then leaps all at once, like a manager, a van or a bigger space
**Flat:** barely moves, like your brand, systems and know-how
cards.callout: Profit scales when you fill each jump before taking the next, and keep in-step costs from creeping up.

cards.title: Same company, smarter growth
body: Two changes. Add clients only in existing neighborhoods, so travel and supplies stay at 10%. And grow to 24 cleaners before hiring a second manager.
Revenue reaches $1.2 million and profit jumps to **$200,000**. Each new dollar since the start kept 17.5 cents.

cards.title: Scale has costs and ceilings.
body: The manager's salary arrives months before the cleaners who justify it, so cash dips before profit rises.
Stretch one manager too far and quality slips. Lost clients can cost more than the saving.
And when wages grow with every job, margins have a ceiling. Scale helps a labor-heavy business. It doesn't turn it into a different one.

cards.title: Now it's a bookkeeping firm.
body: Your firm does monthly books for small businesses. Five bookkeepers each handle about 25 clients. You want to double your clients. Which plan scales best?

options.text: Take any small business that calls, in any industry
options.feedback: You win clients fast, but each new industry brings its own setup and questions. Clients per bookkeeper falls, so staff costs grow faster than revenue.

options.text: Focus on restaurants and build standard checklists so each bookkeeper handles about 35 clients
options.feedback: Costs grow slower than revenue because each person serves more clients. The trade-off is a narrower market to sell into.

options.text: Hire a senior manager and lease a bigger office now, ready for three times the clients
options.feedback: You'll need that jump someday. Taking it before the clients arrive means paying for empty capacity while you fill it.

cards.title: Growth adds revenue. Scale is when costs fall behind.
body: Before you grow, ask which costs will rise in step, which will jump, and how you'll fill each jump.
**Try it today:** compare this year with last year. Divide extra profit by extra revenue. If it's below your overall margin, find the cost that jumped.
